children: The SEC proposed rescinding Rule 613 and requiring SROs and broker-dealers to report substantially the same CAT data to the Commission or its designee. SEC proposes direct control of CAT reporting
Would shift CAT governance from the participant-administered system to the SEC, changing regulatory oversight and the funding framework.
SROs and broker-dealers would report substantially the same data
The proposal preserves core reporting requirements, limiting the stated change to how and to whom CAT data is reported.
Congressional appropriations would fund SEC CAT costs
Could change who bears CAT operating costs; the release gives no projected funding amount or comparison.
Comments open 60 days after Federal Register publication
The proposal is not final; the comment process and any subsequent rulemaking will determine implementation.
Prior changes cut projected annual CAT costs by over $100M
This is a prior projected reduction, not a newly announced saving from the proposal.

This is a proposed regulatory restructuring following earlier CAT cost and privacy changes, not a final rule. A larger catalyst would require the SEC to finalize the proposal after the comment period and disclose implementation and funding details.
